rules.quote: Keep branches focused on the current functionality.
rules.rule: Keep the current branch focused on its existing functionality; do not mix unrelated changes into it.

rules.quote: If the user asks for a code improvement unrelated to the branch being worked on, warn them before proceeding.
rules.rule: When the user requests a code improvement unrelated to the branch being worked on, warn the user before proceeding with it.

rules.quote: Before implementing any change, check whether it belongs to the current branch's scope.
rules.rule: Before implementing any change, check whether it belongs to the current branch's scope.

rules.quote: If not, flag it and let the user decide.
rules.rule: If a requested change does not belong to the current branch's scope, flag it to the user and let the user decide whether to proceed.

rules.quote: Never commit directly to `main`.
rules.rule: Never commit directly to the main branch; every change must be made on its own dedicated branch.

rules.quote: must go on its own branch and be merged into main only when the user explicitly agrees.
rules.rule: Put every change (feature, fix, refactor, chore, doc update) on its own branch, and merge it into main only when the user explicitly agrees.

rules.quote: Before any `git add` / `git commit`, confirm the working branch is not `main`.
rules.rule: Before running any git add or git commit, confirm the current working branch is not main.

rules.quote: If it is, create a branch first.
rules.rule: If the current working branch is main, create a new branch before making any commit.

rules.quote: Only merge to main when the user says so
rules.rule: Merge changes into main only when the user explicitly says to.

rules.quote: When a version bump corresponds to a GitHub milestone, include the milestone URL in the CHANGELOG entry header or description.
rules.rule: When a version bump corresponds to a GitHub milestone, include the milestone URL in the CHANGELOG entry header or description.

rules.quote: check whether a milestone was created for that body of work. If so, link it
rules.rule: When writing a new CHANGELOG entry, check whether a GitHub milestone was created for that body of work, and if so, link it.

rules.quote: Benchmark numbers ("9.6 ms → 11.2 ms (1.17×)")
rules.rule: Do not include benchmark numbers in commit messages.

rules.quote: Binary or artefact sizes
rules.rule: Do not include binary or artefact sizes in commit messages.

rules.quote: Test pass/fail counts
rules.rule: Do not include test pass/fail counts in commit messages.

rules.quote: Disk usage figures, memory deltas, throughput numbers
rules.rule: Do not include disk usage figures, memory deltas, or throughput numbers in commit messages.

rules.quote: put measurements in the spec's
rules.rule: For spec-driven work, put measurements in the spec's "## Measurement (close-out)" section rather than in the commit message.

rules.quote: Reference the spec from the commit if needed:
rules.rule: When needed, reference the relevant spec from the commit message.

rules.quote: a short prose paragraph on the change
rules.rule: Keep the commit body to a short prose paragraph on the change.

rules.quote: a bullet list of files touched and what each contains
rules.rule: In the commit body, include a bullet list of files touched and what each contains.

rules.quote: any non-obvious *why* that wouldn't be evident from reading the diff.
rules.rule: In the commit body, include any non-obvious why that would not be evident from reading the diff.

rules.quote: A bare statement like "tests pass" is also redundant
rules.rule: Do not include bare statements like "tests pass" in the commit body.

rules.quote: Reserve the commit body for content the diff can't communicate.
rules.rule: Use the commit body only for content the diff cannot communicate.

rules.quote: add a detailed `// FIXME:` comment and defer the fix to a future branch
rules.rule: When a code quality issue is noticed mid-iteration in code that the current iteration did not touch, add a detailed `// FIXME:` comment and defer the fix to a future branch.

rules.quote: fix it immediately (it's in scope)
rules.rule: When a code quality issue is noticed mid-iteration in code that the current iteration added or modified, fix it immediately.

rules.quote: check git blame / the current diff to determine if the code belongs to this iteration or predates it
rules.rule: Before fixing anything flagged as a quality issue, check git blame or the current diff to determine whether the code belongs to this iteration or predates it.

rules.quote: Use 100-column line limit for all C/C++ code, not 80.
rules.rule: Use a 100-column line limit for all C/C++ code, not 80.

rules.quote: Always run `clang-format -i` after editing C/C++ files
rules.rule: After editing C/C++ files, always run `clang-format -i` on them.

rules.quote: Methods of up to 4 lines with no loops may be defined inline in the struct/class definition.
rules.rule: A method of up to 4 lines with no loops may be defined inline in the struct/class definition.

rules.quote: Everything more complex goes out-of-line in the `.cc` file.
rules.rule: Any method that is more complex than a short loop-free method (has loops or is more than 4 lines) must be defined out-of-line in the `.cc` file.

rules.quote: Before writing a method body in a header, check: does it have a loop? Is it more than 4 lines? If yes to either, put it in the `.cc`.
rules.rule: Before writing a method body in a header, check whether it has a loop or is more than 4 lines; if yes to either, put the method in the `.cc` file instead.

rules.quote: All infinite loops (exited via `break` or `return`) must use `do { ... } while (true)`.
rules.rule: Write every infinite loop (one exited via break or return) as `do { ... } while (true);`.

rules.quote: Never use `while (true)`, `while (1)`, or `for (;;)`.
rules.rule: Never write infinite loops as `while (true)`, `while (1)`, or `for (;;)`.

rules.quote: Any time an infinite loop is needed, write `do { ... } while (true);`.
rules.rule: Whenever an infinite loop is needed, write it as `do { ... } while (true);`.

rules.quote: The `m_` prefix is acceptable for private and protected members of a `class`.
rules.rule: Use the m_ prefix only on private or protected members of a class.

rules.quote: Never use it on `struct` fields
rules.rule: Never use the m_ prefix on struct fields.

rules.quote: if it's on a `struct` field, drop the prefix
rules.rule: When an m_ prefix appears on a struct field, remove the prefix.

rules.quote: Put an empty line between every method in a class body, including one-liners.
rules.rule: When writing or editing a class body, put an empty line between every method, including one-line methods.

rules.quote: Any time writing or editing a class — constructors, operators, accessors, all of them get a blank line separator.
rules.rule: When writing or editing a class, put a blank line separator around constructors, operators, and accessors as well, not just ordinary methods.

rules.quote: Use `-` (hyphen) instead of `_` (underscore) in all project filenames
rules.rule: Use hyphens (-) instead of underscores (_) as word separators in all project filenames, including specs, docs, and test .cc files.

rules.quote: Any new file in `specs/`, `tests/`, or elsewhere should use hyphens as word separators.
rules.rule: When creating any new file in specs/, tests/, or elsewhere in the project, use hyphens as word separators in the filename.

rules.quote: All identifiers — rule names, variables, functions, types — must be readable by an average human who is not a compiler expert.
rules.rule: Make all identifiers (rule names, variables, functions, types) readable by an average non-expert human.

rules.quote: No unexplained abbreviations.
rules.rule: Do not use unexplained abbreviations in identifiers.

rules.quote: Write `str_literal` not `str_lit`
rules.rule: Name string literal identifiers as str_literal, not str_lit.

rules.quote: Write `float_literal` not `float_lit`
rules.rule: Name float literal identifiers as float_literal, not float_lit.

rules.quote: Write `lex_grammar` not `lg`
rules.rule: Name lexer grammar identifiers as lex_grammar, not lg.

rules.quote: When in doubt, use the full English word.
rules.rule: When unsure whether an abbreviation is clear, use the full English word in identifiers.

rules.quote: Universally understood short forms are fine: `src`, `dst`, `buf`, `idx`, `pos`, `loc`, `op`, `lhs`, `rhs`.
rules.rule: Short forms src, dst, buf, idx, pos, loc, op, lhs, and rhs are acceptable in identifiers.

rules.quote: Do not commit after completing a task unless the user explicitly says to commit.
rules.rule: Do not commit changes after completing a task unless the user explicitly asks you to commit.

rules.quote: Make changes, format, then stop. Let the user decide when to commit.
rules.rule: After making changes and formatting them, stop and leave committing to the user.

rules.quote:
The cost of spelling out "the module" instead of "M" is
 two words
rules.rule: Do not rely on single-letter parameter names (such as M, F, B, V) in code comments or documentation; refer to the entity by its type-noun (e.g., "the module", "the function", "the basic block", "the value") instead.

rules.quote:
Code comments and documentation must read on their own, without the reader
needing to glance at the function signature for context.
rules.rule: Write code comments and documentation so they are understandable on their own, without requiring the reader to look at the function signature.

rules.quote:
If a comment really needs to name a specific parameter, write it out:
  "every function in `module` that has a body" reads fine and disambiguates
  if there's more than one candidate noun in scope.
rules.rule: When a comment must name a specific parameter, write the full parameter name (e.g., `module`) rather than its single-letter form.

rules.quote:
The LLVM-style single-letter parameter *names* themselves
 remain acceptable
rules.rule: Single-letter LLVM-style parameter names may still be used in code itself; the restriction applies only to comment text.

rules.quote: Any analysis, notes, or commentary I write belongs in the `[AI]` section.
rules.rule: Place any analysis, notes, or commentary written into a spec file in the `[AI]` section, not in the human's section.

rules.quote: When asked to fill in or append to a spec file, write content under the `[AI]` section, not inline with the human's text.
rules.rule: When asked to fill in or append to a spec file, write the content under the `[AI]` section, not inline with the human's text.

rules.quote: Prefer `std::string_view` over `std::string` wherever the data is not owned by the object holding it.
rules.rule: Prefer std::string_view over std::string wherever the data is not owned by the object holding it.

rules.quote: Default to `std::string_view` for function parameters, token fields, and any struct member that references data owned elsewhere.
rules.rule: Default to std::string_view for function parameters, token fields, and any struct member that references data owned elsewhere.

rules.quote: Only use `std::string` when the object must own its own copy of the string.
rules.rule: Only use std::string when the object must own its own copy of the string.

rules.quote: Do not push to GitHub unless the user explicitly says "sync" (or equivalent).
rules.rule: Do not push to GitHub unless the user explicitly says "sync" or an equivalent request.

rules.quote: Commit freely, but never run `git push` unless the user asks to sync.
rules.rule: Commit code freely without asking for permission.

rules.quote: never run `git push` unless the user asks to sync.
rules.rule: Never run `git push` unless the user asks to sync.

rules.quote: Capitalise the first character of every TEST_CASE description string.
rules.rule: When writing or editing a Catch2 TEST_CASE description string, capitalise its first character.

rules.quote: if the description starts with a language keyword (e.g. `if/else`, `::name`), leave it lowercase
rules.rule: When a TEST_CASE description starts with a language keyword (e.g. `if/else`, `::name`), leave its first character lowercase.

rules.quote: uppercase the first letter unless it is a language keyword.
rules.rule: When writing or editing TEST_CASE descriptions, uppercase the first letter unless the description starts with a language keyword.

rules.quote: Use `std::unordered_map` for all symbol tables (variable maps, function registries, etc.) going forward.
rules.rule: Use std::unordered_map for all symbol tables (variable maps, function registries, etc.) going forward.

rules.quote: Any new map keyed by string name (variable, function, type) should default to `unordered_map`.
rules.rule: When creating a new map keyed by string name (variable, function, type), default to std::unordered_map.

rules.quote: Existing `map` instances should be migrated opportunistically when touching the surrounding code.
rules.rule: When touching code that contains existing std::map instances, migrate them to std::unordered_map opportunistically.

rules.quote: Tests are #1 priority.
rules.rule: Treat writing and maintaining tests as the top priority in the work.

rules.quote: write failing tests first, then implement, then refactor together.
rules.rule: Follow strict TDD order for each implementation step: write failing tests first, then implement, then refactor together with the user.

rules.quote: When a new feature is requested, expect to write tests first.
rules.rule: When a new feature is requested, write tests before writing any implementation.

rules.quote: Do not jump to implementation before there are tests.
rules.rule: Do not write implementation code before tests for it exist.

rules.quote: If the user approves work before tests exist, gently flag it.
rules.rule: If the user approves work before tests exist, gently flag that the tests are missing.

rules.quote: don't skip it.
rules.rule: Do not skip the collaborative refactor pass.

rules.quote: `tests/explore/` is for experimentation only
rules.rule: Use `tests/explore/` only for experimentation, never for tests tied to a spec.

rules.quote: any test tied to a spec must live in the main `tests/` directory
rules.rule: Place any test tied to a spec in the main `tests/` directory, using a numbered filename such as `test-0014-arrays.cc`.

rules.quote: Set up the `tests/explore/` directory
rules.rule: Set up the `tests/explore/` directory at the start of each new iteration.

rules.quote: an opt-in `pinp_explore_tests` CMake target at the start of each new iteration
rules.rule: Set up an opt-in `pinp_explore_tests` CMake target at the start of each new iteration.

rules.quote: At iteration close, each explore file is either promoted (moved into a numbered test file in `tests/`) or deleted.
rules.rule: At iteration close, either promote each `tests/explore/` file into a numbered test file in `tests/` or delete it.

rules.quote: All C++ code must pass clang-tidy before commit.
rules.rule: Ensure all C++ code passes clang-tidy before committing it.

rules.quote: Run `scripts/lint.sh` to check.
rules.rule: Run `scripts/lint.sh` to check C++ code against clang-tidy.

rules.quote: Immediately after `git worktree add ...`, symlink the install dir from the canonical
rules.rule: Immediately after running `git worktree add` for a new parserkg/ worktree, symlink third_party/llvm-install from the canonical worktree's third_party/llvm-install.

rules.quote: If the build dir was already configured before the symlink, wipe and re-configure:
rules.rule: If the build directory was already configured before the llvm-install symlink was created, run `rm -rf build && cmake -S . -B build` to wipe and re-configure it.

rules.quote: Verify the configure output names the local install and version
rules.rule: After configuring, verify that the cmake output names the local LLVM install and its version, not the system LLVM.

rules.quote: fix and re-configure before
rules.rule: If the configure output reports a different LLVM version than the local install (e.g. a distro-packaged LLVM), fix the symlink and re-configure before building.

rules.quote: Same fix as the install dir — symlink from the canonical worktree:
rules.rule: For a new worktree, replace the empty third_party/llvm-project directory with a symlink to the canonical worktree's third_party/llvm-project.

rules.quote: rmdir third_party/llvm-project   # remove the empty placeholder
rules.rule: Before symlinking llvm-project in a new worktree, remove the empty third_party/llvm-project placeholder directory with `rmdir`.

rules.quote: you would never edit `llvm-project/` per-branch anyway
rules.rule: Do not edit the llvm-project/ source per-branch in a worktree.

rules.quote: run `git submodule update --init third_party/llvm-project` inside the worktree instead
rules.rule: If a worktree needs a divergent LLVM source state, run `git submodule update --init third_party/llvm-project` inside that worktree instead of symlinking.

rules.quote: must not live in `jit.cc` long-term
rules.rule: Do not keep built-in constant injection in `jit.cc` long-term.

rules.quote: it needs to move into `CodegenContext`
rules.rule: Move built-in constant injection into `CodegenContext`.

rules.quote: anything that both paths need belongs on `CodegenContext`, not on `PinpJIT`
rules.rule: When designing codegen APIs, place anything that both the JIT and AOT paths need on `CodegenContext`, not on `PinpJIT`.

rules.quote: Do not jump to other features without addressing these first.
rules.rule: When starting the next iteration, do not work on other features until items 1–4 from near-code-improvements.md (scope duplication, parser state stack fragility, magic operator chars, and codegen.cc size) have been addressed.

rules.quote: When resuming work, pick up from the open items above.
rules.rule: When resuming work on the parser-rewrite branch, pick up from the open items listed in its status file.

rules.quote: Next sema checks go in the appropriate `Sema::check()` overload.
rules.rule: When adding a new semantic check, put it in the appropriate `Sema::check()` overload.

rules.quote: Pinp strings must use a custom struct (not std::string)
rules.rule: Implement Pinp strings as a custom struct, not as std::string.

rules.quote: The layout must be defined as an LLVM struct type usable in both JIT and AOT codegen.
rules.rule: Define the Pinp string layout as an LLVM struct type that works in both JIT and AOT codegen.

rules.quote: `is_heap=0, is_mutable=1` — illegal, never constructed
rules.rule: Never construct a Pinp string with is_heap=0 and is_mutable=1.

rules.quote: Strings are immutable by default
rules.rule: Make Pinp strings immutable by default.

rules.quote: mutable strings always heap-allocated (no mutable inline)
rules.rule: Always heap-allocate mutable Pinp strings; never store a mutable string inline.

rules.quote: Layout must be committed to before codegen is written
rules.rule: Finalize the string layout before writing any string codegen.

rules.quote: **How to apply:** When user returns to this, implement a `scripts/bootstrap.sh` that handles the full submodule setup
rules.rule: When the user returns to the pinp LLVM bootstrap automation task, implement a `scripts/bootstrap.sh` that handles the full LLVM submodule setup.

rules.quote: and a GitHub Actions workflow that caches `third_party/llvm-install/` to avoid full rebuilds on CI.
rules.rule: When the user returns to the pinp LLVM bootstrap automation task, also implement a GitHub Actions workflow that caches `third_party/llvm-install/` to avoid full rebuilds on CI.

rules.quote: give the union a member name (e.g. `u`)
rules.rule: When working on PinpStr in lib/immutable-string.hh, give its anonymous union a member name (e.g. `u`) to eliminate the -Wgnu-anonymous-struct warning.

rules.quote: update all access sites in `lib/immutable-string.cc` and `lib/immutable-string.hh` to use `str_.u.heap.ptr` / `str_.u.inl.tag_len` etc.
rules.rule: After naming the PinpStr union, update all access sites in lib/immutable-string.cc and lib/immutable-string.hh to go through the named member (e.g. str_.u.heap.ptr, str_.u.inl.tag_len).

rules.quote: Do this fix at the start of the next strings iteration, before adding new string features.
rules.rule: Do the PinpStr anonymous union fix at the start of the next strings iteration, before adding any new string features.

rules.quote: This is acceptable while it's the only semantic optimisation.
rules.rule: While the str-concat optimisation is the only semantic optimisation, it may remain inline in emit(BinOpNode).

rules.quote: extract all such logic into a separate AST rewrite pass
rules.rule: When a second semantic-level transformation is introduced, extract all semantic optimisation logic into a separate AST rewrite pass.

rules.quote: runs after sema and before codegen
rules.rule: The semantic optimisation pass should run after sema and before codegen.

rules.quote: The str-concat flattening should be the first thing moved there
rules.rule: When extracting semantic optimisations into a pass, move the str-concat flattening into that pass first.

rules.quote: likely introducing `StrConcatNode` into the AST at that point
rules.rule: When the str-concat flattening is moved into the semantic optimisation pass, introduce a StrConcatNode into the AST.
